solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ring head about one dope

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: the head goes about, around, the letter for one

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring, head spinning, has been doped.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for a narcotic drug, and an opiate is one derived from opium.

clue.text: Where to put post and support shrub

parts.note: a pillar is a column that supports a structure
box is an evergreen shrub used for hedging

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: put in a post to hold up a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: A PILLAR BOX is the red cylindrical postbox found on British streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A British street postbox is where letters are put for collection, so it is where to put post.

clue.text: A recluse hosts male welfare worker once

indicators.note: the recluse hosts, takes in as a guest, the letter for male

parts.note: a loner is someone who keeps apart from others, like a recluse

explanation.surface: A hermit invites a man in, which turns out to be a social worker of old.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was formerly a hospital social worker, and before that a distributor of alms.

clue.text: I must display energy in different ways

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
the phrase asks for energy given a second time in another form: go means energy, vim

explanation.surface: A demand that I should show vigour in many varied ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Energy is supplied twice, 'in different ways': once as the symbol E, once as GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, what a person means when saying I.

clue.text: This writer's pursuing very old man's case

indicators.note: the setter's words follow, chase, the earlier pieces, so they come after them

parts.note: cat is slang for a man, a chap; the 's reads as is, joining to the definition
the setter refers to himself, so this writer has becomes I've

explanation.surface: The writer is chasing up an elderly gentleman's legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is grammatical: the form of a noun used to address someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The vocative is a grammatical case in Latin and other languages, used for direct address.

clue.text: A piece of oral evidence turns up describing part of mouth

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading the letters bottom to top, backwards
only a part of the words oral evidence is taken, run across the word break

explanation.surface: Some spoken testimony emerges in court about part of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Velar is a phonetics adjective for sounds made against the soft palate, the velum, at the back of the mouth.

clue.text: Committee adviser bridles at pundit

indicators.note: the adviser bridles, harnesses round the head, the word at

parts.note: a mentor is a trusted adviser

explanation.surface: A committee's adviser bristles at some media know-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridles' looks like 'takes offence at'; here it means puts a bridle on, enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an expert who gives opinions in the media, as a commentator does.

clue.text: Single-digit growth worried one in the end

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in the word for the end

parts.note: the tail is the end part of something

indicators.note: worried letters are shaken about, so the word one is rearranged

explanation.surface: Sounds like an economist fretting over a feeble one-figure growth rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single-digit growth' reads as an economic statistic; the digit is a toe, and 'worried' signals the jumble of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail grows on one digit of the foot, so this is a growth on a single toe.

clue.text: Food item with rocket on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, the rocket is placed on top of, before, the other piece

parts.note: the V-1 was a German flying bomb, a rocket of the Second World War
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: A dish served with rocket leaves sprinkled on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocket' wants to be the salad leaf; it is the V-1 flying bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A viand is an archaic word for an article of food.

clue.text: Marine line's pump

definitions.meaning: the load line painted on a ship's hull
a light canvas gym shoe, called a pump in Britain

explanation.surface: A sailor's rope runs through a bilge pump.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plimsoll line marks a ship's safe loading depth, and a plimsoll is also a canvas sports shoe.

clue.text: Woman possessed a nut found among bananas

indicators.note: the pieces are found inside, among the letters of, the word for bananas

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, mad
in printing a nut is an en, a space half an em wide

explanation.surface: A woman is obsessed with nuts hidden in a bunch of bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' is a printer's term for an en space.
explanation.definitionFit: A maenad was a frenzied female follower of Bacchus, a woman seemingly possessed.

clue.text: Does salt always stick to this big dish?

definitions.text: Does salt always stick to this big dish?

parts.words: Does salt always stick to this big dish?
parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, who sticks to the main, the high seas, on his course; also the principal plate of a meal

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether salt clings to a large serving plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is a sailor and 'big dish' the principal course of dinner; a sailor keeps to a course across the main.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal dish of a meal is its central serving, the one with most substance.

clue.text: Arrange scores or bust judge

parts.note: the bust is the chest, the upper front of the body
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A musician must sort out the music or face ruin before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like 'go broke'; here it is a noun, the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate is to arrange music for an orchestra, writing out its scores.

clue.text: Second pin number maybe in A&E

indicators.note: the identity code goes inside the letters of the hospital department

parts.note: A&E is the accident and emergency department, taken as its letters
a PIN, personal identification number, is an example of ID

explanation.surface: A nurse in casualty asks for a patient's second PIN.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is a British hospital's casualty department.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is an assistant, as at a duel; an aide likewise helps a principal.

clue.text: In Yorkshire, the tavern that provides lifts?

parts.note: Yorkshire dialect shortens the to t'
a bar is a drinking place, a tavern

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire pub that gives its customers a ride home.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a ski tow with a bar shaped like the letter T, pulling skiers uphill.

clue.text: Yield from a mine drilling copper overdue

indicators.note: the mine drills into, goes inside, the chemical symbol for copper

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a pit is a coal mine
something overdue is late

explanation.surface: A mining report: copper output from the drilling is behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender, and to capitulate is to give up to an opponent.

clue.text: Author's lyrical work lacking effort

definitions.note: author is, the 's being a link

indicators.note: the lyrical work is lacking, without, the word for effort

parts.note: poetry is lyrical writing
a try is an attempt, an effort

explanation.surface: A writer's verse is criticised as lazy and lacking in effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer of tales and poems.

clue.text: Garrulous, like a TV lunatic absorbing atmosphere

indicators.note: the rearranged letters absorb, take in, the abbreviation for atmosphere
a lunatic arrangement is a crazy one, so the letters of like a TV are rearranged

parts.note: at is the symbol for the technical atmosphere, a unit of pressure

explanation.surface: A chatterbox who babbles like a mad television presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunatic' rearranges LIKEATV, and 'absorbing' takes AT into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garrulous and talkative both describe someone who chatters at length.

clue.text: Former Bond loaded with what's needed for passion

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the bond is loaded with, filled with, the word for sex appeal

parts.note: cement bonds things together
it is sex appeal, the quality needed to be attractive

explanation.surface: An old James Bond actor is packed with the charisma romance needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former Bond' suggests an ex-007; 'it' is old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is strong feeling or arousal, a kind of thrilled agitation.

clue.text: Fatuous one follows papers to do with hearing

indicators.note: the numeral for one follows, comes after, the papers

parts.note: identity papers are ID
the Roman numeral for one is I
otic is an anatomy adjective meaning relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A foolish character reads the newspapers on the subject of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatuous means silly and pointless, the same as foolish or stupid.

clue.text: Twice loses unemployment benefit? Just that!

definitions.text: Twice loses unemployment benefit? Just that!

indicators.note: the word for twice loses, drops, the letters of the abbreviation

parts.note: twice the amount is double
UB is the abbreviation for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Someone loses their jobless payment twice and is left with just the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the result is itself the dole, unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: The dole is the British informal name for state unemployment payments.

clue.text: Put off foreign one wearing old hat

indicators.note: the old hat wears, carries round, the foreign word for one

parts.note: old hat means out of date, dated
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A foreigner was deterred from wearing an outdated hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like headgear but means out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Daunted means discouraged, made fearful, so put off doing something.

clue.text: Runner goes around a Munro

indicators.note: the runner goes around, encloses, the letter a

parts.note: a ski is a runner, as on a sledge

explanation.surface: A jogger circles one of Scotland's high mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Munro' suggests a Scottish peak over 3,000 feet; it is the writer H. H. Munro.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki was the pen name of the short-story writer Hector Hugh Munro.

clue.text: Last pair abandoning fashionable, ill-fated mission

indicators.note: the final two letters leave the word for fashionable

parts.note: a la mode means in fashion

explanation.surface: The final couple quit a trendy but doomed venture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was a Texan mission besieged in 1836, its defenders all killed.

clue.text: Bar culture somehow related to consumption

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of bar culture are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Pub culture is in some way bound up with heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumption' looks like drinking; it is the old name for tuberculosis.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumption is an old name for tuberculosis, so tubercular means relating to it.

clue.text: Audibly demonstrates contempt for sauce

indicators.note: audibly says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a crowd boos to show contempt

explanation.surface: Someone loudly scorns a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The sauce is slang for alcoholic drink, as in being on the sauce.

clue.text: Ray comes across right word to help concentration

indicators.note: the ray comes across, spans, the abbreviation for right

parts.note: a manta is a large ray fish

explanation.surface: Ray finds the right word to help him focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name; it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or sound repeated in meditation to focus the mind.

clue.text: To surpass in work, I trust mobile

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: mobile letters move about, so I trust is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to outdo their colleagues at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' is the anagram signal, not a phone; 'work' is the Latin opus, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to go faster or do better than another, to surpass them.

clue.text: Sort of square rings on top of that

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler, a sort of square
two rings are two letter Os

explanation.surface: A dull type wearing rings as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Too means in addition, also, as on top of that does.

clue.text: Firm in the past briefly occupying island

indicators.note: the shortened word occupies, sits inside, the island

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: once means formerly, in the past

explanation.surface: A company that once had a base on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun but is the adjective solid; 'briefly' docks the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete means solid and definite, as a firm offer or concrete proposal.

clue.text: Missing leader, draws lots

indicators.note: the word for draws misses its leading, first letter

parts.note: to doodle is to draw idly, so draws gives doodles

explanation.surface: A team without its captain makes a draw in a lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws lots' reads like a lottery; 'lots' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, lots and lots.
